scope_and_lifecycle_reasoning: EO9799 contains one operative delegation with an express activation date, November13,1946, distinct from the November8 signature. Its title and adjacent EOs9800/9801 are excluded from the inventory. The words authorize and direct the Secretary to exercise statutory authority to classify positions which are to be occupied describe continuing delegated competence; no one-time completion, deadline, sunset or reporting event terminates it. The original recipient is the Secretary of State, not a subsequently abolished named council or temporary post. The expanded named-office/function search yields independent leave authority in EO10471, specific creation/abolition of the German High Commissioner under EOs10062/10608, and class3/4 compensation comparisons in foreign-assistance orders. None withdraws the general classification delegation; the separate office abolition is not a first end for this order. Full EO12292 section10(b) expressly revokes EO9799, and section11 expressly fixes February15,1981 rather than the February23 signature or February25 publication. Full EO12293 delegates new functions under the1980Act with the same effective date and supplies no revival of the old authority. The current USC mention is the historical revocation, not a current predicate. On this bounded record, February15,1981 is the first supported end of the sole unit and whole order. This is a producer candidate pending independent review; no universal statutory exhaustion or human certification is claimed. Provisional status remains no.
savings_reasoning: The sole original command delegates and directs ongoing exercise of classification authority, effective November13,1946; it has no sunset, completion trigger, independent saving or separate lasting command. EO12292 sections10(b) and11 revoke the whole order effective February15,1981 without a target-specific saving. EO12293 grants separate 1980 Act functions effective the same date and does not revive the old delegation. EO10471 leave powers and foreign-assistance orders using class3/4 compensation are independently sourced functions, not saved EO9799 commands. EO10062 fixes one particular new office at class1 and EO10608 later abolishes that office; neither alters the general delegation. Completed classifications, pay consequences and independently authorized personnel acts are not declared invalid by this finding; no examined source identifies a surviving independent command of EO9799 or later revival. No actual savings text tied to this target appears in the bounded numbered-order, named-function and current-law searches.
